messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode pricing follow-up

Tom - great speaking earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

- Use case: customer support triage + automated summarization for enterprise tickets (English, US/EU customers).
- Traffic profile (from call): ~120k messages/month, typical request size ~600 tokens, expected peak concurrency ~45 qps during commerce hours, average qps ~6.
- Data residency: primary US, some EU data must remain in EU region.
- Timeline: pilot in ~6-8 weeks, production in 3-4 months contingent on procurement.

Key question we discussed: preferred deployment mode - Hosted API (pay-as-you-go), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), or Private (VPC/on-prem). You mentioned procurement prefers a committed capacity price for budgeting but engineering is leaning toward Hosted for initial velocity.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll send a concise cost model with three scenarios (Hosted per-token estimate, Dedicated reserved commit pricing + overage, Private/VPC lift-and-shift ballpark).
2) Please confirm: expected 95th percentile concurrency during peak, and whether the EU subset (~15% of traffic) requires a separate private deployment or just regionally-hosted instances.
3) If procurement wants an SOW and draft pricing to start approvals, confirm the buyer contact and PO cadence.

I'll attach a first-pass cost model for Acme that lays out per-token costs, committed GPU monthly compares, and an example reserved commit structure (e.g., 4x A100-equivalent reserved nodes with monthly commit + overage rates).

Thanks - aim to get this over to you by Monday.

--

Thanks Aditya - that matches my notes. A few clarifications from procurement/engineering:

- Concurrency: 95th percentile closer to 55 qps for peak windows (we see short spikes).
- Traffic split: ~85% US, ~15% EU. EU data must be stored in-region but we don't require a separate private deployment for EU if you can guarantee regional isolation and KMS in EU.
- SLA/uptime: procurement will need 99.9% for production; pilot can be lower.
- Procurement contact: Laura Bennett (laura.bennett@acmecorp.com) - she'll own SOW/PO and will request committed pricing vs per-token for budgeting.

For the pilot we'd be happy to try Hosted if the cost is reasonable, but the finance team will need a consolidated committed-cost scenario for months 1-12 so they can evaluate CAPEX/OPEX. Please include a sample reserved-commit plan (monthly commit tiers and overage).

If you can include an example mapping (e.g., X tokens/month ~= Y committed GPUs) and cost per 1M tokens under Hosted vs Dedicated committed, that will help speed review.

--Tom
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Corporation
tom.reilly@acmecorp.com

Tom - thanks for the quick clarifications. Attached is the Acme_Redwood_Cost_Model_v1.xlsx (first pass) and a short draft SOW (SOW_Draft_Acme_Redwood.pdf) so Laura has something to start procurement conversations. High-level notes from the workbook:

- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) estimate: assuming 120k requests/month at 600 tokens/request -> ~72M tokens/month. Using our curated model with median per-token cost, ballpark ~ $0.85- $1.10 per 1k tokens (final depends on model variant and quantization). Monthly spend estimate: $61k- $79k.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity) scenario: example commit = 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved. Monthly commit price (example tier) = $34k/month (committed), with overage billed at a reduced per-token-equivalent rate. This structure often becomes more economical once sustained throughput > ~40k requests/month at the request sizes you shared. I've included a sensitivity table that shows crossover points at different utilization levels.

- Private/VPC: higher one-time onboarding and a base infra fee; best fit if you need on-prem or strict network isolation. For EU-residency-only needs, regional Dedicated + EU KMS is usually simpler than full on-prem.

Attachments: Acme_Redwood_Cost_Model_v1.xlsx (workbook with scenarios), SOW_Draft_Acme_Redwood.pdf (draft). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcmeCostModel

Proposed next steps:
- Quick 30-min review with Laura + finance to walk the cost model (we can run sensitivity during the call). Suggested times: Tue 13th 10:00-11:00PT or Wed 14th 09:00-10:00PT.
- If procurement prefers a committed quote, we can convert the Dedicated scenario into a formal quote and start an internal approvals thread.

Marissa and Neha - looping you in to validate the assumptions on GPU sizing and the crossover math. I flagged the sensitivity table on tab 'Crossover' in the workbook.

Love to hear any quick feedback before I share the files with Laura.
